claims.text: The material family is multiphase AlxCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys with 1 < x < 2.
Aging at approximately 400–600 °C will produce a ductile-brittle-ductile transition as aging time increases.
The proposed non-monotonic ductility transition is driven by competition between B2 precipitation and subsequent B2 coarsening or dissolution into a disordered matrix.
The initial AlxCoCrFeNi microstructure contains both disordered FCC and ordered B2 phases.
Significant short-range order and local chemical order are present in the initial AlxCoCrFeNi alloy.
Intermediate-temperature thermal treatment can induce phase evolution in AlxCoCrFeNi alloys.
A sharp phase-separation transformation occurs at approximately 600 °C.
For x = 1, the B2 ordering temperature exceeds 1220 °C.
The relevant B2 precipitates are Ni-, Co-, and Al-rich, whereas the disordered matrix is Fe- and Cr-rich.
Local and short-range chemical ordering induces coherent nanometer-scale B2 precipitates during short aging treatments.
Fine coherent B2 precipitates strengthen the matrix by precipitation hardening while preserving ductility.
B2 precipitate coarsening and loss of coherency cause an intermediate reduction in ductility.
A shift toward a BCC/B2-dominant matrix can reduce ductility relative to an FCC matrix.
Further B2 coarsening, matrix reordering, or stabilization of another deformation mechanism can restore ductility at long aging times.
Tensile failure strain will follow a U-shaped dependence on aging time, with a distinct intermediate minimum.
The proposed transition is restricted to 1 < x < 2 because B2 is thermodynamically stable but kinetically evolvable in that composition range.
The transition is not expected for x = 0 because that alloy is single-phase FCC.
The transition is not expected for x = 2 because that alloy is fully ordered B2 and its phase fraction does not evolve dynamically in the proposed temperature window.
B2 order is lost near 1400 °C for x = 1 but remains strong up to melting for x = 2.
CrCoNi exhibits short-range order correlated with mechanical properties and has high cryogenic damage tolerance.

contradictions.description: The proposed 400–600 °C aging window is described as being above a temperature at which B2 order is fully stable, but the stated ordering temperature is greater than 1220 °C; 400–600 °C is not above that value.
The temperature window includes 600 °C, while the conditions simultaneously require aging to remain below a sharp transformation temperature of approximately 600 °C.
